references.text: Describes the same event where Satan gains influence over Judas before he receives the bread, and Jesus knows what is happening.
Jesus is troubled in spirit and testifies that one of the disciples will betray him, which leads directly to the entry of Satan in verse 27.
Jesus predicts that Peter will deny him, parallel to how in verse 27 he predicts and instructs Judas to carry out the betrayal quickly.
Matthew recounts the same moment where Jesus identifies the traitor by giving him the bread, and Judas responds to Jesus' words.
Luke confirms that Satan entered Judas before he went to the chief priests, which is the direct action described in John 13:27.
The immediate consequence of Jesus' command in verse 27: Judas leaves the feast immediately after receiving the bread.
